evals.name: one-page-outside-the-repo-and-a-terminal-list
evals.expected_output: It prints the one `git diff HEAD` command it reads, loads show-me with the Skill tool, and writes a single HTML page under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/diff-explain/` — never inside the repo — with a summary, a change map, sections grouped by behaviour that lead with a pseudocode diff or another show-me view — real code visible only for look-closely lines, public signatures, schema or config, boundary checks and very short hunks, at most about 15 lines a section, the full hunks in a collapsed Source block — and a 'look closely here' list of at most seven pointers. All prose on the page and in the reply follows ASD-STE100 — simple approved words, active voice, sentences of at most 25 words — while code, identifiers and paths stay as written. It opens the page and replies with the path and that list as plain `file:line — reason` lines. It edits no source file.

evals.name: an-empty-diff-writes-no-page
evals.expected_output: It reports no changes in `git diff --cached`, writes no page, and records `empty`. It does not fall back to the unstaged diff or to the last commit, which would explain a change nobody asked about.

evals.name: show-me-missing-is-a-named-stop
evals.prompt: /r:diff-explain HEAD~1..HEAD — the show-me skill is not installed
evals.expected_output: It stops, says show-me is missing and how to add it, writes no page and records `no-show-me`. It does not draw the views itself and present the result as this skill's page.
